report.program: Free primary and behavioral health care
report.priceScope: Illustrative whole-recipient accounting cost per 10 Chicago-MSA QALYs

acceptance.evidence: Independent original-source and arithmetic audit; work/geography-handoff-20260913/resumed-20260929/chicago-seven-nine-source-audit.json. Accepted only as illustrative alpha recipient-accounting scenario, not calibrated expected value or qualified donation recommendation.

what: OIPCC provides free primary and behavioral care to uninsured and underserved adults, using staff, volunteer clinicians and institutional partners. The whole clinic is the recipient.
Illustrative central annual Chicago-MSA QALYs: 3.675000; model assumptions are uncalibrated.
Illustrative cost per 10 MSA QALYs: $2,886,493; not a marginal donation price.
strengths: Original audit preserves donated-resource and support costs.
Primary sources identify the recipient and Chicago care site.
reservations: Causal health and gift additionality are judgments.

sections.what: OIPCC provides free primary and behavioral care to uninsured and underserved adults, using staff, volunteer clinicians and institutional partners. The whole clinic is the recipient.
sections.monitoring: The undated current website says more than 2,500 patients; it does not establish annual unique patients. N=2,500 is a rounded panel proxy, and k=.5 is an explicit judged annual treated fraction. Pairing that current panel with FY2024 costs is a cross-period proxy, not observed annual productivity. Request a dated annual unique-patient count, symptom/function response, sustained utility and alternative care.
sections.qualitative: Continuity of medical and behavioral care could relieve symptoms and prevent deterioration, but no recipient causal QALY evidence was located. The model values one bounded morbidity pathway; referral benefits and mortality are not separately credited. Donated resources make cash costs a poor substitute for economic resource costs.
sections.cost: FY2024 audited whole-clinic expense is $1,060,786, retaining management and fundraising. Recognized nonfinancial contributions appear as $660,816 on the activity statement and $660,815 in note 3: a $1 discrepancy and a mislabeled table-year heading are retained as source caveats. They already have matching expenses and are not added again. The scenario uses 2,500 panel proxy × .5 annual treated fraction × .30 additional responder share × .05 utility × .5 year × .4 funding additionality × .98 MSA share.
sections.funding: The FY2024 audit reports revenue $1,304,302, government grant $263,484 and ending net assets $1,107,740. It records recognized donated care but excludes volunteer contributions that fail recognition criteria. No priced unfunded expansion was found. FY2023 and FY2022 audited expenses are $1,181,581 and $1,436,262.

Current patient panel and volunteer description

model.counterfactual: a is the share with meaningful morbidity relief beyond equivalent alternative care; b separately discounts replacement funding and constrained volunteer capacity. No mortality benefit is credited.
model.attribution: One morbidity pathway only. Other health pathways are provisionally assigned zero net benefit, not demonstrated zero or a lower bound. Visits, prescriptions and retail care values are not added as QALYs. Cross-recipient benefits cannot be summed without person-level deduplication.
model.uncertainty: All utility, causal response, duration, funding additionality and residence parameters are illustrative judgments, not measured causal effects, calibrated expected values, confidence intervals or marginal gift purchase prices. Different accounting treatment of donated care prevents comparative economic-efficiency rankings.
sensitivity: Poor and favorable scenarios vary several uncalibrated assumptions together; they are not exhaustive bounds.
Zero additionality produces zero QALYs and no finite price.
Changing cost alone scales price proportionally; changing any multiplicative benefit factor inversely scales price.
At otherwise central assumptions, k=.25/.5/1 yields half/base/double benefit. Current panel and FY2024 expenses are unmatched in time.
missingInputs: Recipient causal morbidity and health-utility outcomes with follow-up and alternative-care comparison.
Additional unrestricted dollars, priced unfunded expansion and binding staff/volunteer constraints.
Patient residence, overlap across services and clinics, and incremental economic cost of donated resources.
Dated annual unique-patient count and matched cost/activity year.
model.costScope: Full FY2024 audited recipient expense, including recognized nonfinancial resources and support costs. Unrecognized volunteer time and external partner costs remain outside accounting expense; accounting value is not opportunity cost.
model.geographicAttribution: Clinic at 5425 W Addison Street, Chicago, anchors service in Cook County within the pinned 13-county Chicago MSA. g=.98 is judged residence share, not measured; Kenosha is excluded.
model.nativeOutcomes: Current panel exceeds 2,500, but an annual denominator was not established; annual activity is modeled with k, not asserted observed.

scenarios.label: Illustrative central
scenarios.assumptions: N=2500; k=0.5; a=.30; u=.05; T=.5; b=.4; g=0.98. Judged benefit conversion, not measured EV.

scenarios.label: Illustrative poor case
scenarios.assumptions: k=0.25; a=.1; u=.02; T=.25; b=.2; g=.9. No probability assigned.

scenarios.label: Illustrative favorable case
scenarios.assumptions: k=1; a=.5; u=.08; T=1; b=.7; g=1. Not an upper bound.

scenarios.label: No additional health benefit
scenarios.assumptions: b=0: all care replaced or constrained; zero benefit, no finite price.
